content.text:
I built `index.html`: a heatmap with one row per sensor depth (2 m at the top, 40 m at the bottom) and one column per month from Feb 2018 to Dec 2025. Each cell's colour is that month's mean temperature in °C. It renders with no errors or warnings.

The caption is worked out from the data when the page loads. It says that at 2 m, monthly means range from 1.3 to 19.3 °C and are warmest on average in September. At 40 m they stay between 0.7 and 10.9 °C and peak in October. So the yearly swing gets smaller and later with depth. 18 of the 665 depth-months have no data and are shown as hatched cells.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - monthly mean of daily means via d3.rollup, per depth and month
  R2: done - one column per month, Feb 2018 to Dec 2025, taken from the data's date range
  R3: done - depth-months with no daily rows are hatched grey and listed as "No data" in the legend
  R4: done - rows labelled 2 m to 40 m, in depth order
  R5: done - colour legend titled "Monthly mean water temperature (°C)", ticks in °C
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption whose numbers and peak months come from the data
assumptions:
  - Monthly mean = unweighted mean of the daily means in that month (not weighted by n_obs)
  - Missing means a month with zero daily rows; months with only some days of data still get a cell
  - Months are calendar months in UTC
limitations:
  - A cell can be based on only a few days in a month; the hover tooltip shows the day count
  - The caption's fixed wording ("weakens and lags") rests on the computed 2 m vs 40 m ranges and peak months; it does not re-check intermediate depths
  - The colour scale uses 0–20 °C (data extent rounded); the red-yellow-blue colours are not tested for every type of colour blindness
```
